claims.statement: retail-portfolio is a four-system application: a Python 3.14/FastAPI backend in src/ with SQLAlchemy 2 async models over PostgreSQL and Alembic migrations, a Huey worker on Redis, a SvelteKit 2 / Svelte 5 SSR frontend in frontend/, and a stateless Go indicator sidecar in services/indicator-service/.

Local development is Docker Compose only: the whole stack reads a single root .env copied from the tracked .env.example, and `docker compose up -d` exposes backend on 8001, frontend on 8002, mailcrab on 8003 and the indicator service on 8085, with every port Compose-interpolated from root .env variables.

The frontend service receives JWT_SECRET sourced from the root SECRET_KEY, so the SSR route guard in frontend/src/hooks.server.ts verifies tokens with exactly the backend HS256 signing key and Compose fails fast when SECRET_KEY is unset.
All development commands must be executed inside Docker containers via `docker compose exec <backend|frontend> <command>`; the host environment is never the reference and CI runs the same checks.

`./scripts/agent-test` (shorthand `just test`) is the primary test harness for agents: it runs inside Docker by default, sanitizes output (ANSI stripping, vendor-frame removal) and hard-caps it at --max-chars (default 3000), and enforces Gate 0 (lint + type checker, halting before tests on failure), Gate 1 (a path argument, targeted and fail-fast) and Gate 2 (no path, full suite with an Index/Traces two-tier summary).

The agent test harness accepts the flags --backend, --frontend, --all, --gate0-only, --no-gate0, --local, --json and --max-chars, and the just recipes are thin wrappers over it (just test, test-backend, test-frontend, test-all, check, up).

Editing a backend model mandates generating an Alembic migration in the same change, and migration files must follow the `<hash>_<description>.py` naming convention with manual SQL executed via op.execute() inside a standard revision.

Tests must never depend on external services: backend tests must mock every outbound client (Redis, HTTP APIs such as EODHD and broker APIs, SMTP), frontend tests must mock all API calls, and the ephemeral testcontainers PostgreSQL is the only permitted infrastructure dependency.

Backend domains follow a layered internal structure (models, schemas, repositories, services, api/api_types, routers) in which repositories always return schemas rather than ORM models and services must not raise HTTPException; the error is instead handled at the router boundary.

The backend is organized by business domain — account (accounts, positions, portfolios, institutions), auth, market (securities, prices, watchlists, alerts, notes, documents, indicators, AI), integration (broker gateways), ws (WebSocket fan-out), core (shared exceptions, email, redis, pagination, context) and config — with cross-domain access only through each domain's public APIs.

Parallel agents must isolate work with the git worktree workflow: `scripts/setup-agent-worktree.sh <worktree-path> <branch-name>` creates the worktree and generates a .env with unique ports so each worktree runs its own Compose stack without file or Docker resource conflicts.

Chart drawing tools follow a per-plugin directory layout under frontend/src/lib/components/charts/plugins/<plugin-name>/ (state, mouse, pane-renderer, pane-view, constants, index), share plumbing only through plugins/helpers/, must not import from sibling plugins, and delegate pure financial math to $lib/utils/finance/.

The OpenWiki pages under openwiki/ are generated documentation refreshed by the scheduled .github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml workflow; source code and tests are authoritative and generated pages should not be hand-edited in preference to updating source.

The repository is laid out as routing destinations: `src/` for the FastAPI backend, `frontend/` for the SvelteKit app, `services/indicator-service/` for the Go sidecar, `migrations/` for Alembic revisions (configured as the Alembic script_location), `tests/` for backend pytest suites, `src/stubs/` for stub gateways used by tests and STUB_EXTERNAL_API mode, `src/commands/` for seeding and market-data flush CLI entrypoints, `openspec/` for capability specs and change artifacts, and `scripts/` plus `.github/workflows/` for tooling and CI.

`just up` is the preferred stack-start recipe: it resolves the host Docker socket's group id with scripts/docker-gid.sh and passes it as DOCKER_GID so the backend/worker containers (uid 1000) can reach the daemon, which is what allows testcontainers-backed tests to start throwaway PostgreSQL inside the containers.

Beyond the published service ports, Compose maps the backend and worker debugpy ports to 8090 and 8091 (BACKEND_DEBUG_PORT, WORKER_DEBUG_PORT) and PostgreSQL to 5432 (POSTGRES_PORT), all interpolated from the root .env like the rest of the stack.

CI is a three-job workflow: a backend job running uv run ty check, ruff check + ruff format --check and pytest on Python 3.14; a frontend job running npm run check, npm run lint and npm run test:run on Node 25 with VITE_* and JWT_SECRET env vars; and an indicator-service job running go vet, go build and go test on Go 1.27.

AGENTS.md is the root agent guide that delegates backend work (src/, tests/, migrations/) to src/AGENTS.md and frontend work (frontend/) to frontend/AGENTS.md; CLAUDE.md is only a one-line stub that imports AGENTS.md via `@AGENTS.md` and contributes no guidance of its own.

The OpenWiki block appended to AGENTS.md frames the generated openwiki/ tree as optional just-in-time context rather than required startup reading, states that source code and tests are authoritative so a brief's unknowns and review items are verification gaps rather than automatic requirements, and directs agents to prefer the narrowest quiet validation that proves the changed behavior while preserving complete failure output.

`src/.env` and `frontend/.env` are obsolete: all custom values (frontend VITE_* overrides, backend overrides) must be moved into the single root `.env` and both files deleted, since the backend, worker, Compose interpolation and frontend dev server all read the root file.

The accounts/holdings read path that the quickstart routes to the Accounts & Holdings Views page spans three frontend surfaces: the accounts dashboard at `/`, the account-scoped holdings page at `/accounts/[id]`, and the cross-account `/holdings` page (reachable from the sidebar actions group), whose table columns and stock/company grouping are driven by the persisted `holdings_table` and `holdings_group` preferences.

The security detail workspace the quickstart routes to is backed by per-feature API service modules under `frontend/src/lib/api/` — `notesService.ts`, `documentsService.ts`, `alertsService.ts`, `snapshotsService.ts` and `indicatorsService.ts` — so its actions sidebar groups (indicators, price alerts, notes, documents, AI analysis, holdings) each talk to the API independently.

The realtime surface the quickstart routes to consists of two independent backend WebSocket entrypoints: the user-scoped `/api/ws` router (`src/ws/router.py`) served by the process-global `ConnectionManager` that fans out the `WsEventType` messages over the `ws_messages` Redis Pub/Sub channel, and the Huey dashboard task stream under the `/worker/api/tasks` prefix (`src/worker_dashboard/router.py`).

The persisted user-preferences blob the quickstart routes to is a per-user JSON column on the auth user model exposed through `frontend/src/lib/api/userPreferencesService.ts`, and the quickstart's own linked surfaces consume it: the root layout load reads `sidebar_open`, `collapsed_watchlist_ids` and `watchlist_order`, and the `/holdings` load reads `holdings_table`, `holdings_group` and `elliott_waves`, each falling back to defaults without failing the render.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the same verification the local stack does, in three jobs: backend (`uv run ty check`, `ruff check` + `ruff format --check`, `pytest` on Python 3.14), frontend (`npm run check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test:run` on Node 25 with `VITE_API_BASE_URL`, `VITE_INTERNAL_API_URL`, `VITE_ALLOWED_HOSTS` and a `JWT_SECRET` supplied by the workflow env) and indicator-service (`go vet`, `go build`, `go test` on Go 1.27).

The quickstart's non-negotiables are the set the repository's own guides repeat: Docker-only commands, the agent-test harness gates, the model-edit migration rule, never reaching external services from tests, git-worktree isolation for parallel agents, OpenSpec spec-driven change, and treating the generated `openwiki/` tree as optional just-in-time context rather than authoritative.
